To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the L1 influence on L2 reading is a function of L1-L2 similarity and that this influence is stronger for L2 readers who are less proficient in L2 reading.
L1 reading strategies transfer to L2 reading, and the degree of transfer depends on the nature of L1 reading strategies, L2 reading tasks, and L2 reading proficiency.

the influence of first language (L1) orthographic structure on second language (L2) reading is mediated by the L2 reader’s level of L2 reading skill and that L1 orthographic structure influences L2 reading only when it matches the structure of the L2 orthography.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the L1 in the L2 reading comprehension of adult learners of English as a foreign language (EFL).
the influence of first language literacy on second language literacy.
the nature of the first language influence in second language reading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L1 reading is a process of making sense of the print and L2 reading is a process in which the L2 reader tries to make sense of the print in L1 or the print in L2 (or both).
the influence of the first language is pervasive and significant in L2 reading and the extent of influence depends on a number of factors.
the influence of the L1 on L2 reading is complex and multifarious.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the first language (L1) influences the reading of a second language (L2) in two ways: (1) the L1 reading strategies that are used by the reader and (2) the L1 knowledge that is transferred to L2 reading (Gottlob, 2003) The L1 reading strategies used by the reader are the result of the L1 reading process and the L1 knowledge transferred to L2 are the result of L1 reading experience.
first language reading is an active process of sampling linguistic and contextual cues to produce a hypothesis about the message.
L1 transfer has been a major issue for L2 reading research, and the role of L1 transfer in L2 reading has been examined by many researchers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L2 reading proficiency can be improved through training in L2 word reading, but the extent to which it can be improved depends on the L1 of the reader.
there is a lot of transfer of reading skills from L1 to L2, but that transfer is not automatic.
the first language plays a role in how the second language is learned and used.
